the statistical error of counting measurements at high counting rates is increased over the value predicted by Poisson statistics, and that the increase is caused by overlap of the pulses produced by each X-rays.
the statistical uncertainty in a measurement is increased by pulse overlap and that a conventional dead-time analysis does not correctly predict this increase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for pulse-overlap effects in photon counting detectors, and the use of this model for the calculation of the statistics of the counting rate at high counting rates.
the development of a new model that describes the counting statistics of photon-counting detectors at high counting rate, which is a requirement of modern synchrotron sources.
the development of a new statistical theory of counting statistics for high counting-rate detectors, which includes a correction for pulse overlap.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the counting statistics of a photon-counting detector at high counting rates is not described by Poisson (n(-1/2)), but by Poisson (exp(n/2)), where n is the mean number of X-ray photons incident on the detector per second.
the statistical errors of photon counting detectors at high counting rate are not simply a Poisson (N-1/2) error but are also affected by pulse overlap.

the statistical error associated with a photon-counting measurement is the sum of two contributions: the Poisson error associated with the number of detected X-rays and a contribution due to the overlap of the pulses from individual X-rays, which is a function of the counting rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a photon-counting detector operating at high counting rates is not a counting device, but rather a measuring device that produces a measurement with a statistical uncertainty that depends on the incident X-ray flux.
the statistical uncertainty of the measured counting rate increases with the square root of the counting rate.
the overlap of pulses can be corrected for by the use of a conventional dead-time model, but the statistical errors are not the same as for a Poisson distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the counting rate of a photon-counting detector can be significantly underestimated at high counting rates, and that the statistical uncertainty of an experiment can be over-estimated.
the counting statistics for a photon-counting detector are different at high counting rates than they are for low counting rates.
the counting statistics of a detector at high count rates are significantly affected by the overlap of detector electronic pulses.
